doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ken Burns's Jazz omitting the Lafayette Theater
summary: Teddie and Hank feel the documentary did not go deep enough and left out the Lafayette Theater era.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Would you say that they did a complete story on jazz? They didn't go far back enough I thought. Nothing was mentioned about the Lafayette.
Oh, you’re talking about the Ken Burns thing.
All the famous bands used to come in for at least a week or two. There was Duke Ellington, Cab Calloway. It was like a show downtown when they

didn't have a spotlighted act coming in. I knew I could get a slot. These were all famous musicians there were in the shows. I thought that they should go back as they became famous. This was like, Benny Carter.
Ken Burns covered that but he didn't go into depth. He left out some of the most important things that happened there.
Right. Were you consulted on that at all?
No. I got a cameo mention in it by the way. I thought to say, “Thanks a lot Ken.”
I think the recording you are mentioning was called, "Tip Toe Tap Dance,” that is the solo recording.
